citation: Kaslow, Cahill, and Ayres (2020), Development and Application of the CubeSat System Reference Model
title: Development and Application of the CubeSat System Reference Model
venue_type: conference paper; venue name not explicitly stated in paper.md; DOI metadata provided
modeling_scope: Reusable CubeSat System Reference Model for mission-specific logical architecture of space and ground components. It covers stakeholders, requirements, behaviors/use cases/activities, architecture hierarchy from domain and enterprise to segments, subsystems and components, technical measures, external constraints such as budgets and milestones, and validation/verification. It includes generic CubeSat subsystems such as the Power Subsystem and cites earlier power-usage/energy trade-study work, but it does not present a detailed EPS model.
mbse_language_method_tool: MBSE reference model; SysML-compliant; hosted in a graphical modeling tool; methodology-agnostic. Background tool environment includes No Magic MagicDraw/Cameo Simulation Toolkit, Phoenix Integration ModelCenter and MBSE Analyzer, Analytical Graphics Systems Tool Kit, and MathWorks MATLAB.
robot_platform: CubeSat/nanosatellite mission platform, including CubeSat form factor and CubeSat deployment system accommodation; prior project history applied the model to the Radio Aurora Explorer (RAX) CubeSat.
task_domain: CubeSat mission architecture and system engineering for space and ground components, targeted especially at university CubeSat teams but described as useful for research, government, and commercial teams.
interface: Model/interface coverage includes space and ground components, CubeSat deployer interface requirements, requirement relationships to stakeholders/behaviors/technical measures/V&V, graphical-tool hyperlinks/navigation, requirements tables exportable to spreadsheets, and Word/Excel technical-measure artifacts embedded in the model.
feedback: Technical measures are tracked and assessed, with verification activities providing data to the technical measurement process. Future feedback from university teams using the CSRM is to be evaluated and incorporated into model improvements.
evaluation: The paper demonstrates the CSRM through a notional top-down application outline, diagrams of packages/architecture/V&V, prior application to RAX and trade-study history, formal review/vetting by systems engineering professionals, use by several university CubeSat teams, favorable introduction to CubeSat teams, and submission to OMG as a candidate CubeSat specification. It does not report a quantitative controlled evaluation of claimed outcomes.
rq_relevance: RQ1: yes, because the paper presents a reusable SysML/MBSE CubeSat reference model for mission-specific space/ground logical architecture and includes generic power-subsystem and power-usage evidence. RQ2: partial, because outcomes are claimed for CSRM/MBSE reuse, development time, quality, common baselines, sharing, and institutional knowledge transfer, but reliability is not specifically reported and the outcomes are not tied to detailed EPS modeling. RQ3: partial, because the CSRM explicitly models verification and validation activities, procedure/result/status properties, and tracing to requirements/technical measures, but the verification linkage is general system/CubeSat requirement verification rather than EPS-specific verification.
claimed_outcomes: Quality enhancements and economies associated with reusability are claimed for adopting the CSRM.
The reusable model is claimed to reduce development times and increase the quality of CubeSat spacecraft and ground-system design.
Organizations are claimed to be able to extend the model with component libraries, enhancing internal reuse and transfer of institutional knowledge to successive programs.
Conformance/common logical elements are claimed to provide a common baseline for comparing and evaluating mission-specific implementations and for sharing/reuse of design elements.
Reliability outcomes specifically: Not reported. EPS-specific reproducibility or integrability outcomes: Not reported.
verification_validation_linkage: The CSRM includes a Validation Verification package. Requirement elements expose a Verified By property, and requirements can be traced down to validation and verification activities. Verification is defined as inspection, demonstration, test, and analysis of the mission-specific model; a Verification Activity can include plan, procedure, execution notes, results, and status and can be captured as element properties, an activity diagram, or a Word document. Validation activities similarly link to mission objectives/technical measures. No EPS-specific verification procedure is reported.
key_findings: The CSRM is a platform-independent, SysML-compliant MBSE reference model intended as a reusable starting point for CubeSat space and ground logical architecture.

The model structures CubeSat development around five core element groups: stakeholders, requirements, behaviors, architecture, and technical measures, plus an explicit validation/verification package.

The architecture hierarchy decomposes from CubeSat domain and mission enterprise to space and ground segments, CubeSat and ground subsystems, and subsystem components; the generic CubeSat subsystem set includes a Power Subsystem.
The model supports traceability from stakeholders, behaviors, and technical measures to requirements, subsystems/components, and V&V activities.
The CSRM is intended to be methodology-agnostic: teams populate and modify model elements and relationships for their own missions rather than following a mandated method.

Evidence for outcomes is mainly expert vetting, community use, OMG submission, and stated benefits of reuse; the paper does not present measured reliability improvement or EPS-specific verification results.
limitations_gaps: The CSRM provides a library of model elements but does not dictate which elements or relationships to use; the development team must populate the model with maturing elements.
If the five fundamental elements are inconsistent with a team's methodology, the team may need to modify the containment tree to conform with its methodology.
Future feedback is needed to identify value-added model elements not currently in the CSRM, portions of the model that do not function as intended, and new capabilities to add.
Processes for dissemination, configuration control, updates, and available formats after possible OMG specification adoption have yet to be worked out.
Expansion from CubeSats to a broader satellite reference model is presented as a future effort requiring assessment.
No formal threats-to-validity section is provided; limitations are discussed mainly as future work and model-maintenance issues.

quality.rationale: The paper has conference-paper/IEEE DOI metadata and a formal systems-engineering publication style, supporting a credible-venue score. It discusses gaps and future model-improvement needs, but not a formal limitations or validity-threats analysis.
